name: Argentine nationalism
summary: Argentine nationalism puts national sovereignty, economic independence and cultural identity above liberal internationalism, and claims continuity from San Martin through Rosas to Perón. It includes a Catholic, anti-liberal, military-friendly current (the Maurrassian and Hispanist nationalists) and a populist current (FORJA and Peronism) that stresses social justice, class collaboration and a Third Position. Today it centres on the Malvinas/Falklands claim, Antarctic and South Atlantic claims and opposition to foreign economic dependence.
scope: A composite of the 20th-century Argentine nationalist tradition: the Catholic and Maurrassian nacionalismo of the 1930s (Irazusta brothers, Palacio, Lugones's turn, Meinvielle at the traditionalist edge) and the economic-nationalist and Peronist current (FORJA, Perón's Twenty Truths). Answers follow the shared core of sovereignty, economic independence, Catholic-traditional culture and a strong state; where the strands diverge (democracy, Jews, unions, the Church) answers are neutral or low confidence. It excludes liberal civic patriotism and sub-national or Marxist anti-imperialism.

sources.title: Peronism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Third Position, economic independence, organised community, social policy, Catholic influence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Peronism made social assistance one of its two pillars and expanded state health and welfare provision, which the nationalist mainstream inherited.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Perón's social justice programme centred on raising workers' incomes and dignity of labour, so a substantial wage rise fits it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nationalists from FORJA to Perón held that capital must serve the economy and the nation, and blamed free-market liberalism for dependence on Britain.

public-ownership.rationale: Perón nationalised key economic tools such as railways and utilities and the nationalist tradition treats them as strategic national assets.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Redistribution against the oligarchy is a Peronist theme, but the sources discuss taxation little, so this is inferred from social justice.

unions-good.rationale: Trade unions are built into the Peronist movement and its organised community, though Catholic-nationalist traditionalists wanted them corporatively controlled.

property-fundamental.rationale: Justicialism subordinates capital and property to social function, and Catholic nationalists attacked capitalism as the Golden Calf.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Peronism limited multinational firms and heavily regulated the economy, and FORJA opposed foreign corporate control.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social assistance is one of the two named pillars of Justicialism, so cutting welfare contradicts it directly.

worker-ownership.rationale: Perón sought class collaboration with capital kept in the economy, not collective worker ownership of firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Nationalist authoritarian currents favoured order and security over liberal privacy, but the sources do not address surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Catholic-traditionalist moral outlook suggests opposition, though the sources never discuss drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split, since nationalists distrust liberal speech norms but also distrust state speech codes, and the sources are silent.

strong-leader.rationale: Nationalists admired caudillo leadership (Rosas, Perón, Uriburu) and Palacio held that real leadership needs a caudillo representing the people.

state-harmful.rationale: Truth 19 calls for a centralized government and an organized state, so the idea that the state is harmful is flatly opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: The sources never address firearms, and adherents of both strands give no common position.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Army is a carrier of nationalist values and nationalists backed military coups in 1930 and 1955.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Catholic-nationalist moral conservatism implies opposition, though no source addresses it.

decide-locally.rationale: Truth 19 asks for centralized government, and the tradition is unitary and anti-federal in its Rosas-Perón line.

rehabilitation.rationale: Authoritarian nationalists favoured punishment while Peronist welfarism favoured rehabilitation, and the sources do not discuss it.

traditional-family.rationale: Catholic nationalism and Perón's Christian Justicialism treat the family and children as the base of society, with children the only privileged group.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Catholic nationalism would oppose it, though later Peronist governments legalised it, so strands diverge and the sources are silent.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic-nationalist doctrine opposes it, but Peronist politicians are split in modern Argentina.

more-religion-public.rationale: Catholic nationalists wanted public life subordinated to Catholicism, and Perón introduced Catholic teaching in schools.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The sources show a class and nation framing rather than racial redress, so this is inferred, and Truth 4 recognises one class of people.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Catholic traditionalism implies rejection, but this modern question is not addressed in the sources.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement's core concern was defending national identity from dilution and foreign influence, as the 1880s nationalists feared.

gradual-change.rationale: Nationalists backed coups and a radical overhaul against liberal democracy, though they claim to defend tradition.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Fears that European immigration would dilute national identity drove the 1880s nationalism, though Peronism was less restrictive.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Political sovereignty is a Justicialist aim, and nationalists resisted foreign powers' interference.

free-trade.rationale: FORJA opposed British economic dependence, and Peronism sought economic independence by building domestic industry.

nation-first.rationale: Truth 8 puts the Fatherland first in political priorities, and nationalism since FORJA stresses sovereignty over cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Sovereigntist and anti-imperialist outlook and neutrality in the world wars imply scepticism, though not directly stated.

open-borders.rationale: Nationalism rooted in defending national identity and borders rejects open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Developmentalist economic independence favours industrial growth, although the sources do not address environmental limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The tradition never addressed climate change, and no principle gives a clear answer.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No source speaks to this, and nationalists were industrialisers but not technological utopians.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from the drive for national industrial and energy independence, since the sources do not discuss nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nationalists justified the 1930 and 1943 coups and Perón's movement spoke of revolution, though mostly military not popular revolt.

experts-over-public.rationale: Perón's Truth 1 says true democracy is government doing what the people want, and populists distrusted technocratic elites.

central-planning.rationale: Peronism planned and regulated heavily but kept a mixed economy with private capital, so a fully planned economy is not its position.

socialized-markets.rationale: Peronism kept private business alongside state firms and rejected collective worker ownership, and this framing is not addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: The question is a Georgist niche the sources never discuss.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed, and strands split between redistributive Peronism and landowning conservative nationalists.

basic-income.rationale: Truth 5 makes work both a right and a duty, with everyone to produce at least what they consume, which cuts against unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Peronism built domestic industry to cut reliance on foreign economies, and tariffs were its main tool.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Perón controlled the economy through the state and directed investment into strategic national industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Catholic social teaching favours distributed property but the sources do not state this for nationalism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Truth 5 treats work as a right and duty, and Peronism rejects abolishing wage labour as a Marxist aim.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Perón nationalised the central bank and the tradition favours state control of money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Perón organised society into state-linked bodies such as the CGT and business confederation, and Catholic nationalists proposed a corporate chamber.

one-party-rule.rationale: Perón's movement dominated and Truth 8 puts Movement above people, but adherents did not claim a single-party doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Only a minority such as Julio Irazusta favoured monarchy, while the mainstream is republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Maurrassian nationalists said democracy is anti-Catholic and Peronism defined democracy as popular will rather than liberal procedure.

direct-votes.rationale: Peronism claims popular rule but relies on leadership and organised community, and nothing is said on referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Perón's organised community channelled workers through unions inside the state rather than councils replacing parliament.

right-to-secede.rationale: The nationalist tradition is built on unity and territorial integrity of Argentina, so secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Maurrassian nationalists defended elitism and hierarchy and favoured caudillo leaders, though Peronists spoke of popular rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalist currents defended coups, militias such as the Civic Legion and Tacuara, so violence is not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Army promoted nationalist values in wars, but sources do not say adherents hold that war improves character, and Perón sought neutrality.

separate-church-state.rationale: Catholic nationalists wanted public life subordinated to the Church, and Perón brought Catholic teaching into schools.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Meinvielle's traditionalists wanted a theocratic state, but most nationalists and Peronists wanted Catholic values, not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Truth 19 asks for an organized state, and nationalism holds defence to be a core state task.

military-superiority.rationale: The Army and Malvinas claims are core nationalist themes, though Argentina's actual capacity is limited.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Neo-republican nationalists defined race by spiritual unity and baptism rather than blood, so a single ethnic group is not required.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Truth 11 seeks national unity rather than conflict and the movement recognises one class, workers, rejecting class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Peronism pursued social justice and a social function for each person, not strict equality of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: The nationalist tradition celebrated the Conquest of the Desert and national territorial unity, so special indigenous authority is inferred as rejected.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism is strong but reparations are not discussed, and Argentina's own nationalism has Spanish heritage.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalists promoted Hispanidad, a Grand Argentina and a Southern Cone union, backing unity among Hispanic peoples.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalists attacked liberalism and the Golden Calf, and Truth 16 makes capital serve social well-being.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Justicialism balances individual and community rights, and Truth 5 makes work a duty, so community weighs heavily.

limit-population.rationale: Argentine nationalism feared dilution by immigrants not overpopulation, and Catholic doctrine opposes population control.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement promoted industrialisation as the route to economic independence.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not addressed and nationalists value tradition alongside industrial development.

human-enhancement.rationale: Catholic traditionalism implies caution, though sources are silent.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Peronism stresses popular and personal leadership, so this is inferred as rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources are silent on this modern issue.

restore-past-order.rationale: Maurrassian and Catholic strands wanted to restore a lost Hispanic Catholic order while Peronism looked forward to a new Argentina.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Truth 13 holds that a government needs a doctrine, being otherwise a body without a soul.

direct-action.rationale: Nationalists used coups and militias while Peronism used both elections and mass mobilisation.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrial independence is a core aim, so a return to foraging is plainly outside it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Truth 17 gives each person a social function, which presupposes a division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Peronism rewarded work and social function, with each person producing at least what they consume.

production-for-use.rationale: Capital should serve the economy and social well-being, but Peronism kept profit-making private firms.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Peronism held class collaboration between labour and capital, not that profit is exploitation, though it attacked the oligarchy.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Peronism rejects class dictatorship and communism in favour of a third position between Yankees and Marxists.

collective-farming.rationale: Peronism backed an agrarian federation of landowners and was anti-Marxist.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anti-imperialist but not Marxist, and the sources do not state this.

taxation-theft.rationale: The interventionist state and social justice rely on taxation.

harm-principle.rationale: Nationalists and Catholic traditionalists accept state moral regulation beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Truth 15 balances individual with community rights, and nationalists stress community and nation.

conscription.rationale: Nationalism backs the Army and national defence, and Argentina used conscription for a long period.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The idea contradicts the tradition's stress on the Fatherland and political participation of the people.

state-as-business.rationale: The state serves social justice and not customers who can leave.

positive-liberty.rationale: Truth 18 seeks an Argentina that is socially just and economically free, treating material means as a condition of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not address it, though nationalists distrusted liberal academia and press.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Neo-republican nationalists defined race by spirit and baptism, not blood.

organic-representation.rationale: Catholic nationalists proposed corporatist representation and Perón's organised community channelled society through trade bodies.

total-state.rationale: Catholic nationalists and Perón's centralised state were interventionist but the sources do not describe a total state directing everything.

national-rebirth.rationale: Maurrassian nationalists backed the 1930 coup to cure decadence of liberal democracy and Lugones called for a strong patria.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Argentine nationalism claims the Falklands, South Georgia and Antarctica, but as recovery of its own claims rather than general expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal loyalty is a feudal form foreign to a republican tradition, though caudillo loyalty to Perón existed.

bound-labor.rationale: Perón's movement exalted workers' dignity and rights, so bound labour is opposed.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic nationalists treated Thomist doctrine as universal moral truth, though this is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Justicialism's national unity and organised community, and Thomist common good, imply one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Nationalist currents split between Catholic antisemitic strands and Peronist relations with Israel, and no source addresses it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources do not address it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Spanish is already the national language, so the question has no application.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Peronism integrated labour with employers via class collaboration rather than democratic control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Perón's state favoured public schooling including free universities, though Catholic nationalists favoured Church education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Peronism favoured state spending for industrial development and social programmes over austerity.

economic-freedom.rationale: Peronism sought economic freedom for the nation from foreigners, not market freedom as a precondition of liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: The sources do not discuss this.

national-self-determination.rationale: The tradition rests on national sovereignty and Argentina argues for territorial integrity over islanders' self-determination, though it rejects the islanders' claim.

force-without-un.rationale: Argentina invaded the Falklands in 1982 and the tradition does not accept external veto on use of force.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Catholic nationalists subordinated politics to faith and Thomism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from nationalist priority for citizens, since the sources do not address it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Truth 5 makes work both a right and duty, so those who can work are expected to.

class-collaboration.rationale: Perón aimed to balance labour and capital, and Truth 11 prefers national unity to strife.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving national culture and heritage is a core nationalist value.

dominated-front.rationale: Peronism promoted a Third Way and ties with other nations opposing Western domination, and nationalists backed a united Southern Cone.

workers-nation.rationale: Perón's movement united workers within the Fatherland ranked first, and Truth 8 puts Fatherland above all.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Catholic traditional outlook suggests it, though Peronism extended women's suffrage.

ban-interest.rationale: Catholic nationalists attacked capitalism as the Golden Calf, but usury bans are not stated policy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Argentine nationalists defined race spiritually and Peronism recognised one class, so segregation by law is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Peronism saw the state as arbiter between labour and capital, siding with labour but not as a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Peronist nationalism wanted national control of resources and energy self-sufficiency.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Fear of dilution of national identity underpinned the nationalist demand that immigrants adopt Argentine culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources show worry about dilution but not a deliberate plot, so most adherents would not endorse it.

proportional-representation.rationale: The sources do not address it.

national-mission.rationale: Nationalism has Hispanic and Southern Cone unity ideas but no clear mission to spread its government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Peronism extended women's suffrage but nationalists generally reject feminist structural claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Peronism opposed the oligarchy and political circles anti-popular, and FORJA attacked colonial elites.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Army promoted nationalist values in the Dirty War, and defenders resist prosecution.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Perón's state planned and regulated the economy with a large public sector, and Truth 19 asks for an organised state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Neo-republican nationalists defined race by spiritual unity and baptism, and Argentina is a mixed society.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic doctrine and Perón's people-centred ideology support equal dignity, though nationalists hold hierarchy elsewhere.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Peronism is not Marxist, so this internal Marxist debate is outside it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Argentine nationalism celebrates the Conquest of the Desert and Argentine settlement as the founding of the nation.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A unitary national law fits the centralising tradition, though the sources do not address it directly.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Catholic traditionalists may favour the Church but Argentina has religious liberty and the sources do not state it.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Argentina's beef economy makes this plainly outside the tradition.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Perón introduced Catholic teaching into public schools and Catholic nationalists favour it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This is a Marxist-Leninist question and the sources give nothing on it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Truth 1 holds that real democracy means government doing what the people want, implying legitimacy rests on the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Peronism sought economic independence through domestic industry and reduced foreign reliance, in line with a mercantilist export aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Catholic nationalism and Peronism's national unity ideal reject forced expulsion, even though some currents blamed minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nationalists backed coups and militias, and Argentina invaded the Falklands, so no absolute ban on initiating force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Truth 11 prefers unity to strife, and Catholic nationalists attacked liberal competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nationalist regimes banned opponents, but the sources do not address this directly.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-oligarchic and anti-colonial language fits it partly, but the sources do not use this concept.

separated-powers.rationale: Truth 19 asks for centralised government and nationalists criticised liberal checks, favouring caudillo leadership.

vanguard-party.rationale: Truth 2 and 3 make the movement popular in essence, not a disciplined revolutionary vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Truth 12 makes children the only privileged group and Peronism sought social justice for workers.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Peronism backed a constitutional right to housing, but the specific policy is not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Peronism built on union power and the state sided with labour, though it controlled unions inside the movement.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Peronism blamed inequality and dependence for poverty, and Catholic doctrine opposes population control.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Fear that immigration would dilute national identity suggests cohesion is linked to cultural homogeneity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hierarchical and elitist nationalist doctrine rejects lotteries for office.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Nationalists supported Uriburu's suppression of constitutional rights and military regimes in emergencies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Peronist governments froze retail prices and gave food subsidies to workers.

party-controls-media.rationale: Peronism controlled media at times, but the sources do not give doctrine for it.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Army is seen as an independent guardian of the nation, not a party's tool, even though Perón came from the military.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Concern about dilution of national identity implies caution on citizenship, though not stated directly.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Peronism had populist anti-elite rhetoric, but this specific demand is not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Truth 3 demands that a Peronist serve the Movement, though party rules are not stated.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Political sovereignty is a core aim, and nationalists resist supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nationalists favour strong executive authority and caudillo leadership, with Argentina's president as commander-in-chief.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic nationalists accept hierarchical Church governance, as Catholic doctrine already provides.

clerical-rule.rationale: Meinvielle's traditionalists wanted theocratic subordination, but most nationalists and Peronists did not want clerics governing.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Truth 8 puts the Fatherland first, so defeatism is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Catholic traditionalism supports moral censorship, though the sources do not state it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Perón's 1949 constitution allowed re-election and caudillo-style leadership is endorsed by nationalists.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources are silent on the recall mechanism.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Neutrality in World War II and Third Position outlook favour avoiding blocs, though Argentina had no major alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Peronism backed a right to housing but not abolishing renting, and private property remained.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nationalists value the professional Army as guardian of the nation.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Some nationalists idealised the countryside and gauchos, but Peronism was urban industrial and the sources are silent.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Nationalists seek a Grand Argentina and a Southern Cone union, implying support for reunifying lost parts of the historic viceroyalty.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist anti-oligarchic and anti-liberal elite rhetoric attacks colonised intellectuals, as in FORJA's critique.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalists and Catholic traditionalists regard Hispanic Catholic civilisation as higher than liberal Anglo-Saxon one.

death-penalty.rationale: Authoritarian nationalism leans to it, but the sources do not address it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Catholic nationalism implies opposition, though not addressed in sources.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Catholic nationalists would not primarily push this and sources are silent.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Catholic moral traditionalism supports it but the sources do not discuss it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Neo-republicans defined the nation spiritually through baptism and Argentina uses birthright, so descent-only citizenship is not their position.

minority-language-support.rationale: Unitary national culture implies low priority, though not stated.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Catholic nationalists favour Catholic primacy, so exemptions for minorities are not their priority.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's liberal idea is foreign to Catholic traditionalist communitarianism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Economic independence and anti-imperialism imply support for cancelling foreign debt, as Perón repatriated the debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Truth 18 and the Peronist flags demand an economically free Argentina, and FORJA's motto says colonial Argentina wants to be free.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Perón rewrote the constitution in 1949, but the sources do not give a general rule on assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Nationalists backed authoritarian rule over liberal democracy to restore national strength.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The sources show no doctrine and nationalists prioritise their own country.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Argentina pursued nuclear programmes but the sources do not state a position.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Truth 1 and Perón's popular legitimacy favour direct choice by the people, and Argentina's president is directly elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Perón nationalised the central bank and subordinated the economy to state direction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Argentina's constitution calls its sovereignty over the Falklands legitimate and non-prescribing, refusing concessions.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Truth 16 says capital serves the economy and the economy serves social well-being, and Truth 15 balances individual and community rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources do not address Soviet classification.

collective-defense.rationale: Argentina historically avoided blocs, but the sources give no stance.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Argentina calls Britain's 1833 reassertion an illegal act of force, treating annexation without consent of the previous authorities as unlawful.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Catholic nationalists want public life subordinated to the Church not the reverse.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Perón was both head of state and leader of a movement, and nationalists prefer a leader who embodies the people.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: National unity and territorial integrity are central, so force against secession is accepted.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary tradition implies against special regimes, though not addressed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Argentine nationalism is republican and Catholic, with no divine ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Peronism favoured redistribution, so a flat tax conflicts with its social justice aim.

character-from-environment.rationale: The sources do not address it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Neo-republicans stressed constitutional order and Peronists legal institutions, even with strong executives.

space-expansion.rationale: The sources do not mention space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Maurrassian traditions favoured hierarchical corporatist mixes but there is no stated stance.

leader-cult.rationale: Peronism built a public cult around Perón and Evita with portraits and mass praise.

equal-parenting.rationale: The sources do not address it.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist question, and Peronism rejects class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Peronism backed an agrarian federation of landowners, though it taxed agricultural exports, so splits over breaking up estates.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not address it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Argentina's territorial claims rest on inheritance from Spain and continental shelf rather than co-ethnics living abroad.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Catholic nationalists value Catholic primacy but Argentina has religious liberty and punishing apostasy is not stated.

women-must-cover.rationale: Foreign to Catholic Argentine culture, and Perón extended women's suffrage.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary sovereignty belongs to the economic independence aim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalists promote Hispanidad and a Southern Cone union among peoples of shared language and heritage.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A unitary national culture is preferred, though not explicitly addressed.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources do not address it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Catholic nationalists see spiritual factors as primary, and Peronism rejected Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Perón sought to dismantle the elite's capitalism and limit multinational firms.

no-bailouts.rationale: State-directed economies often rescue strategic firms, but the sources do not address it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Populist nationalists reject liberal institutions constraining the popular will, as Truth 1 treats democracy as doing what the people want.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Catholic traditional outlook, though Peronism (Evita) promoted women's political participation, and the sources are silent.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Peronism sought economic independence through domestic industry, though the bloc idea is not specific to it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The sources do not address it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Truth 5 stresses dignity of work, but material incentives remained in Peronism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Tacuara-style groups existed but this is a Guevarist idea not stated by mainstream nationalists.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Truth 7 calls feeling superior oligarchic and Truth 12 makes children the only privileged group.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalists contest historiography to centre San Martin, Rosas and Perón, and teach national tradition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-imperialist FORJA claimed colonial Argentina wanted freedom, opposing tutelage by advanced powers.

patriotic-education.rationale: The Army and nationalists promoted national values and loyalty, and Perón's movement placed Fatherland first.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The sources do not address racial preferences in Argentina.

notes: Strands diverge sharply: Catholic integralists (Meinvielle) and Maurrassians reject democracy and some blamed Jews and Freemasons, while Peronists embrace mass politics and unions. Several answers are therefore medium or low confidence, and many modern social questions are inferred.
